![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/5f2a88925bb122972e72141202dbca14db9c82b9b3182f0786ca4981b127560e.png)

Which of the diagrams above shows three collinear points?
question.worked_solution:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

- Diagram I shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/a2632fa133ec55c1db7987c799ab0654f06dc6f919daea9d2c8121dad5a12341.png)

- Diagram II shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/ab431babe2ab9b5fc1707ca12c91b1f8b3dbd0ccdc102e9ff090980d65052d6c.png)

- Diagram III shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/5adac57025cae294be0b8bc83a3905b4275d1bcd92b92ad6c126b3d1b108302f.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
